title: Hourly slab conversion - HC fragility workbook
content:
Summary:
Small workbook to evaluate converting on-demand hourly/spot billing into slab commitments and the implied headcount fragility (how many FTEs we'd need to hire/bench across 3 pricing elasticity regimes). Focused on burst-heavy customers who cause big hourly spend variance. Draft — numbers rough; want feedback from SRE/Platform before finalizing.

Top-level assumptions (explicit):
- Baseline token throughput (prod) = 110M tokens/day across hosted API
- Current hourly/spot GPU cost blended = $4.75 / GPU-hour (after discounts)
- Slab tiers proposed: Starter (50 GPU-hrs/day), Scale (250 GPU-hrs/day), Wave (1,000 GPU-hrs/day)
- Commitment discount multipliers: Starter = 0.88, Scale = 0.76, Wave = 0.62 (approx relative to on-demand)
- Operational leverage: 1 FTE infra engineer supports ~200 GPU-hrs/day steady-state (assumes SRE automation level 0.7)
- Hiring lead time: 10 weeks for infra/ops with ramp to full productivity at 14 weeks
- Target buffer for SLA safety: +15% capacity for regional failover

Quick conversion table (weekly view) - placeholder numbers:
| Week | On-demand GPU-hrs | Proposed slab mix (Starter/Scale/Wave hrs) | Implied committed hrs | Delta vs on-demand hrs | Notes |
|------|------------------:|--------------------------------------------:|----------------------:|-----------------------:|------|
| 0 (now) | 3,360 | 3,360 (all on-demand) | 0 | -3,360 | baseline - no commitment
| 4 | 4,800 | 2,400 / 1,600 / 800 | 4,800 | 0 | pilot customers onboarded to slabs
| 8 | 7,200 | 4,000 / 2,400 / 1,200 | 7,600 | +400 | modest overcommit to absorb bursts
|12 | 9,600 | 5,500 / 3,200 / 1,500 | 10,200 | +600 | expected seasonal peak prep

Headcount fragility matrix (convert committed hrs to infra FTEs):
- Formula: FTE_needed = ceil((committed_gpu_hrs / 24) / 200 * (1 + fragility_factor))
- Fragility factor is a hand-coded multiplier representing emergency headcount slack (0.0 = perfect automation, 0.25 = fragile)

Example scenarios (Week 12):
- Low fragility (0.0): committed hrs 10,200 => (10,200/24)/200 = 2.125 => 3 FTEs
- Medium fragility (0.15): effective = 2.125 * 1.15 = 2.44 => 3 FTEs (still 3 but less buffer)
- High fragility (0.4): effective = 2.125 * 1.4 = 2.975 => 3 FTEs (but close to 4 in real rounding rules if on-call overhead counted)

Pricing sensitivity block (per-customer marginal impact):
We model three elasticity bands for customers converting to slabs:
- Sticky (inelastic): 70% convert to slab, usage remains ~95% of prior on-demand (value-seeking but stable)
- Opportunistic: 40% convert, usage drops 20% (customers optimize away waste)
- Churn-risk: 20% convert, usage remains same but margin pressure increases due to discounts

Per-customer example (annualized):
- Customer A (Sticky): Annual on-demand spend = $420k. After slab discount (weighted average multiplier 0.74) => $310k (savings to customer = $110k) => Redwood revenue delta = -$52k (assume pass-through of 60% of savings to Redwood in net margin changes) but unit-cost decreases by 24% improving gross margin if utilization increases.
- Customer B (Opportunistic): Annual on-demand spend = $300k. After slab + optimization usage drop = spend $180k => immediate revenue down -$120k but backend cost falls by $145k (higher relative CPU efficiency) => unit econ may improve, net margin +$25k.
- Customer C (Churn-risk): Annual on-demand spend = $120k. Accepts a slab to maintain predictable pricing => spend $95k; Redwood absorbs majority of discount due to contractual terms => small margin compression -$8k annually.

Platform/Cash implications (high level):
- Short-term (0-3 months): Cash outflow increases due to prepayments/credits for slabs. Need a working capital buffer of ~1.2x projected slab credit issuance (estimated $1.1M) to avoid runway pressure.
- Medium-term (3-12 months): If utilization improves by >10% across committed pools, incremental GM lifts 200–450 bps depending on model mix.
- Risk: If conversion skews toward churn-risk cohort, realized revenue could drop >8% in worst-case while capacity commitments remain baked in.

Operational triggers and playbook (draft):
- Trigger 1 — Utilization < 65% across committed pools for 3 consecutive weeks: freeze new slab sales; open re-negotiation lane for opportunistic customers; accelerate marketing to sticky segment.
- Trigger 2 — Headcount pressure (hiring pipeline < 2 months for infra): pause slab upsell for Wave-tier; route new interest to dedicated capacity (longer-term contracts).
- Trigger 3 — Cash buffer draw below $600k: restrict staggered slab prepayment terms, require monthly settlement for new customers.

Open questions / validation required (SRE/Product/Legal):
- What is the true operational support ratio per 24/7 slab vs on-demand (SRE to GPU-hours)? We used 200 GPU-hrs/FTE but that may vary by model family and region.
- Can Platform guarantee a fast redeploy path that reduces fragility factor to <0.10 within 12 weeks?
- Legal: are there constraints on how much credit we can front for slab pilots to enterprise customers (contract phrase review needed)?
- Billing: how will credits and refunds be handled for burst-usage over slab ceiling? (tiered overage rates?)

Next steps (near term):
- Run a 6-customer pilot: pick 2 sticky, 2 opportunistic, 2 churn-risk candidates; run 8-week slab pilot with telemetry (utilization, churn signals, post-conversion net revenue). Owner: Ethan (pilot ops) — start wk of 2026-11-22.
- Create a micro-sim (Monte Carlo) for 1,000 sampled customer mixes to estimate 90% downside distribution. Owner: Priya/Finance modeling — due 2026-12-10.
- SRE to validate 200 GPU-hrs/FTE assumption and provide per-region variance. Owner: Sara — due 2026-11-19.

Notes to self / draft log:
- This is intentionally messy: want quick iteration with product and SRE.
- Keep close to commercial on pricing language: we should present slabs as "commit + burst" to reduce perceived risk.
- Consider a 6-month time-limited "convert-back" clause for early pilots (reduces legal friction).

Raw numbers (copyable) for modelers:
- Baseline daily GPU-hrs (global): 3,360 -> monthly ~100,800.
- Slab discount multipliers: Starter 0.88, Scale 0.76, Wave 0.62.
- Buffer factor for SLA: 15%
- Hiring lead time: 10 weeks, full productivity 14 weeks.

If you read this and want changes: add comments inline or drop a note in #fin-pricing channel.

-- Priya
